core_claims.claim: The Planning Data API exposes planning and housing datasets through a consistent interface.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
Geometry and point values are represented as WKT in entity responses.
Pagination links include next, previous, first and last URLs.
The API publishes an OpenAPI document at the documented openapi.json endpoint.
Dataset pages support bulk downloads in multiple formats.
Entity search results can be downloaded from the search interface.
Planning Data distinguishes dataset records from individual entities.
Dataset specifications define required field names for provider submissions.
Provider data can be supplied through OGC WFS or ArcGIS API endpoints where a specification allows it.
Records for legal documents require a direct document-url field.
Published endpoints require a documentation-url for each record.
Planning Data accepts official planning-authority web publication as a source route.
Guidance states that live feeds can be hosted by GIS or open-data platforms.
Planning Data automatically updates from compliant live feeds.
Alternative source downloads may be presented on dataset detail pages.
Title-boundary entities identify the dataset as title-boundary.
Title-boundary entity pages expose an entity identifier independently of the source reference.
Title-boundary geometry carries Ordnance Survey copyright and database-rights attribution.
Planning Data supports integrating the API with web and back-office systems.
The API documentation describes date filtering as part of the query contract.
The API documentation describes geometry-based filtering as part of the query contract.
Response links are intended to be followed rather than reconstructed from offsets.
Bulk download availability does not itself prove an exact candidate response was read.
A title-boundary entity example cannot establish the exact three target references without target-specific readback.
Dataset-level schema verification is distinct from authoritative candidate identity binding.
WKT geometry availability does not by itself provide measured elevation values.
Numeric height-difference promotion remains unsupported until candidate-specific boundary and elevation evidence are read.
